_note: Real-NBA reference targets for docs/design/phase-1-simulation-engine.md §10's validation harness (tools/validate_sim.py, tests/integration/test_sim_validation.py). Per §10's own decision ('reference targets live in seeds/nba_reference_distributions.json with source and season fields, not hardcoded in Python'), every metric below carries its own provenance rather than one blanket citation for the whole file, because two different provenance tiers are mixed here on purpose: 4 metrics (possessions_per_48, efg_pct, tov_per_100_poss, fta_per_fga) were confirmed against a live web search this round and are the tightest-trust numbers in the file; `starter_mpg`/`rotation_bench_mpg`/`deep_bench_mpg` are copied verbatim from `phase-1-step-7-calibration.md` §10.1's already-closed decision; everything else is general basketball knowledge for the 2023-24 season, stated as approximate and flagged for tightening against a primary source in a later pass. `band_low`/`band_high` are this harness's actual pass/fail gate -- deliberately wide (this stage exists to catch gross miscalibration, e.g. an engine producing 25% eFG% or zero turnovers, not to certify NBA-identical realism; that finer tuning is step 11's job). **Correction (critic round 24, B24-1): 4 entries are derived/non-independent, not 3 as the round-23 fix claimed** -- `seconds_per_possession` (`1440/possessions_per_48`, see its own note), `dreb_pct` (`1 - oreb_pct`, an algebraic identity of `tools/validate_sim.py`'s own aggregation formula, not an engine property), `share_fga_mid` (the remainder after `share_fga_rim`/`share_fga_three`, since all 3 shot-mix shares sum to exactly 1.0 by the same aggregation formula), and `deep_bench_mpg` (constrained by the 240-team-minutes-per-game identity against `starter_mpg`/`rotation_bench_mpg` at this harness's 14-player-per-team roster size). All 4 are kept as separate JSON entries rather than removed, because each still reads a real (if non-independent) harness output and the report format has no 'informational' row type; a reader should not treat the naive '27 metrics' or post-fix '26 gating metrics' count as independent findings -- it is closer to 22. Percentages are stored as 0-1 fractions, not 0-100, throughout. **BDA-6.3 addition (docs/design/block-defender-attribution.md): `blk_per_game` and `top_shot_blocker_bpg` are two new, genuinely independent gating entries** -- nothing else in this file reads `blk`, so neither is derived from an existing band the way the 4 above are; the file's own historical '27'/'26'/'22' counts above predate this addition and are not restated here.
band_rationale: Every metric's band is a relative width around a stated reference value: +/-15% for FT% (a historically low year-to-year variance stat), +/-20% for most rate/percentage stats (pace, eFG%, zone FG%, shot-mix shares, TOV/100, PF/game, FTA/game, top-scorer PPG, win-total SD uses +/-25%), +/-25%-30% for derived/remainder or looser-variance stats (mid-range share, p90 PPG), and +/-40% for small-magnitude or structurally noisier shape stats (p10 PPG, share of players over 30 mpg) where a fixed relative width would otherwise be too tight to survive normal seed-to-seed variance. `starter_mpg`/`rotation_bench_mpg`/`deep_bench_mpg` use the exact bands `phase-1-step-7-calibration.md` §10.1 already closed, not an independently-chosen width. `dreb_pct`'s band is the arithmetic complement of `oreb_pct`'s band (1 - `oreb_pct`'s bounds, reordered) -- **corrected (critic round 24, B24-1): this is exact by the harness's own aggregation formula (`dreb_pct = 1 - oreb_pct` identically), not merely 'nearly complementary,' and the prior wording's 'engine's own Tier-2 invariant' framing was a false attribution — Tier-2 invariants are steps 4-5's possession-chain identities and have nothing to do with this harness's rebound aggregation.**

seconds_per_possession.source: derived from possessions_per_48 (1440/99.0), not independently sourced
seconds_per_possession.note: FIXED (critic round 23, B23-1): the prior 29.09/[24.24,36.36] figures used 2880/pace, which is the wall-clock interval between one team's own consecutive possessions -- not what tools/validate_sim.py measures. The harness accumulates total_seconds once per game but team_possessions_raw once per team_box_line (i.e. twice per game), so `total_seconds / team_possessions_raw` = 2880 / (2 x per-team pace) = 1440 / possessions_per_48. Reference and band are 1440/99.0 and 1440/possessions_per_48's own band (79.2, 118.8), inverted (1440/118.8 = 12.12, 1440/79.2 = 18.18) -- these now actually overlap the range a correctly-paced engine produces, unlike the prior band.

oreb_pct.note: REVISED (critic round 23, B23-4): raised from 0.225 to ~0.24, closer to recalled 2023-24 league rebounding totals (~10.6 ORB / ~33.0 DRB per team per game, implying ORB% ~0.243); 0.225 reads closer to the 2017-19 trough and ORB% has climbed since. p90_ppg_rotation.note: REVISED (critic round 23, B23-6): raised from 19.5 to ~24.5. The pool is every rotation player (>=15 mpg) league-wide, roughly 240-270 players; a 90th-percentile cutoff over that pool sits near the near-All-Star tier (~25 players/season score 20+ ppg league-wide), not at ~19-20. Internally consistent with the file's own points_per_game (114.5) and top_scorer_ppg (32.0) references: p90 (~24.5, ~top decile of rotation players) sits meaningfully below top_scorer_ppg (~32.0, the single best scorer in the league).

p50_ppg_rotation.note: REVISED (critic round 23, B23-6): raised from 8.5 to ~11.5. Cross-check against this file's own points_per_game (114.5): the ~8 rotation players (>=15 mpg) per team consume roughly 90% of team scoring, giving a mean rotation PPG of ~0.90 x 114.5 / 8 ~= 12.9; a median of 8.5 implied an implausible 1.5x mean/median skew for a top-8-by-minutes scoring pool. ~11.5 is a more plausible ~1.1-1.2x ratio for a right-skewed but not extreme distribution.
